title: Does joining the loyalty program raise monthly spend?
answer_html: Yes, most likely by about $9 per customer a month, and newer customers gain the most. Treat the exact size with some caution: it assumes nothing important about who joined is missing from the data.
caution_bullets: 1 in 10 customers had few look-alikes to compare with.
A hidden factor 60% as strong as last quarter's spend could erase it.
segment_card_note: Your hunch was right: the gap between the two groups is about $9 (range $6 to $13).
gap_title: Most of the $35 gap isn't the program
gap_text: Members spend $34.77 more a month than non-members. About 73% of that comes from who joined: marketing pushed the program to city customers and people who already spent a lot.
methods_title: Nine methods, one answer: about $8 to $10
methods_text: The main method was chosen before any results. The others are cross-checks, including two foundation models, CausalPFN and TabPFN. They agree, which is reassuring but not proof: they share the same blind spots.
segment_title: Newer customers gain about 2.5 times as much
hidden_note: Only last quarter's spend clears the line. A hidden factor that strong would be unusual, but not impossible; for example, how engaged someone already was.
trust_title: Why the grade is C, not B
dag_note: Confirmed by you before the run.
trap_text: Points redeemed are a result of joining. Treating them as a control flips the answer to a nonsense result.

data_issues.title: Data issue to check
data_issues.text: 966 non-members (44%) show 1 to 10 redeemed points, but only members should have any. It doesn't affect this result, but if some members are recorded as non-members, the true effect could be larger.

next_steps.title: Confirm with a small randomized test.
next_steps.text: Invite a random half of a group of new customers. About 600 customers per group would detect a $5 lift.

questions.title: How did customers end up joining?
questions.text: You weren't sure, so we treated it as self-selected. If marketing targeted people using data we don't have, the estimate could be too high.

questions.title: Can one customer joining affect another's spend?
questions.text: Shared households or referrals would break an assumption. We assumed not.

questions.title: Is margin what matters?
questions.text: This is one month of spend, before the cost of the points.
